extracted.intended_audience: nyc agencies, agency counsel, municipal officials involved in rulemaking and adjudication, and regulated parties
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements in the NYC Charter Chapter 45 (City Administrative Procedure Act) governing agency rulemaking (agenda, notice, review, publication, emergency rules, compilation) and minimum adjudicative procedures. Intended to guide agencies in legally compliant promulgation of rules and conduct of adjudications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Rule' (inclusions and exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Rule" means the whole or part of any statement or communication of general applicability that (i) implements or applies law or policy, or (ii) prescribes the procedural requirements of an agency including an amendment, suspension, or repeal of any such statement or communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule includes statements prescribing: (i) standards which, if violated, may result in a sanction or penalty; (ii) a fee to be charged by or required to be paid to an agency; (iii) standards for the issuance, suspension or revocation of a license or permit; (iv) standards for any product, material, or service which must be met before manufacture, distribution, sale or use; (v) standards for the procurement of goods and services; (vi) standards for the disposition of public property or property under agency control; or (vii) standards for the granting of loans or other benefits. "Rule" does not include: (i) statements relating only to internal management or personnel not materially affecting public rights or procedures; (ii) forms/instructions or explanatory policy statements with no legal effect; (iii) statements concerning allocation of agency resources or personnel; (iv) traffic-regulating statements indicated by signs/signals based on engineering/technical considerations not involving substantial policy considerations; (v) statement effecting a non-continuous street closing; or (vi) certain statements adopted pursuant to specified charter sections. (This definition governs what agency communications must follow the procedural requirements of this chapter.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory agenda contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall publish by the first day of May annually, a regulatory agenda which shall contain:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agenda must include: (1) a brief description of subject areas where rules may be promulgated during the next fiscal year and reasons why action is considered; (2) a summary, to the extent known, of anticipated contents of each proposed rule, its objectives and legal basis; (3) a description of types of individuals and entities likely to be subject to the rule; (4) identification, to the extent practicable, of all relevant federal, state, and local laws and rules, including those that may duplicate, overlap or conflict; and (5) an approximate schedule for adopting the proposed rule and the name/telephone number of an agency official knowledgeable about each subject area. The single-head agencies appointed by the mayor must forward the agenda to the mayor for review for consistency with administration policy objectives. Failure to include an item does not preclude action; if rulemaking is undertaken on a matter not included, the notice of proposed rulemaking must include the reason it was not anticipated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to adopt rules and plain language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency is empowered to adopt rules necessary to carry out the powers and duties delegated to it by or pursuant to federal, state or local law. No agency shall adopt a rule except pursuant to this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each such rule shall be simply written, using ordinary language where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice content and publication timing for proposed rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall publish the full text of the proposed rule in the City Record at least thirty days prior to the date set for a public hearing or the final date for receipt of written comments, whichever is earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proposed rule amending an existing rule must show deletions in brackets and additions underlined or italicized. A proposed repeal must contain the rule in brackets or cite the rule and summarize its contents if in the Compilation. The published notice must include a draft statement of basis and purpose, statutory authority (particular sections/subdivisions), the time and place of public hearing if any or the reason a hearing will not be held, and the final date for receipt of written comments. If the proposed rule was not in the regulatory agenda, the notice must include the reason it was not anticipated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission to officials, news media, and civic organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the full text of the proposed rule shall be electronically transmitted to the office of the speaker of the council, the council's office of legislative documents, the corporation counsel, each council member, the chairs of all community boards, the news media and civic organizations no later than the date the proposed rule is transmitted to the City Record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "News media" includes all radio/TV stations broadcasting in the city, newspapers with city-wide or borough-wide circulation, and any union/trade newspapers affected by the rule; "civic organizations" includes city- or borough-wide organizations, labor unions, trade associations or groups that request notification annually. An inadvertent failure to fully comply with these notice requirements shall not invalidate any rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency website and electronic publicity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall provide information regarding the public hearing to be held with regard to a proposed rule in a prominent location on the agency's website at least seven days prior to the date set for such hearing and shall provide a link to the NYC Rules online portal (or substantially similar successor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies shall, to the greatest extent practicable, publicize upcoming public hearings via electronic means likely to reach interested members of the public. This requirement does not create a private right of action, and inadvertent failure to comply does not invalidate a rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporation counsel review of statutory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The corporation counsel shall review the proposed rule to determine whether it is within the authority delegated by law to the agency proposing the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the corporation counsel determines the proposed rule is not within the agency's delegated authority, the corporation counsel shall notify the agency in writing prior to publication of the final rule in the City Record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law department and mayor's office review, analysis, and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The law department and the mayor's office of operations shall review each proposed rule prior to publication in the City Record and provide stated analyses; after review they shall certify that they have performed such review and transmit the certification and analysis to the relevant agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Law department statements should address whether the rule: (i) is drafted to accomplish the purpose of the authorizing provisions of law; (ii) is not in conflict with other applicable rules; (iii) to the extent practicable and appropriate, is narrowly drawn to achieve its purpose; and (iv) to the extent practicable and appropriate, contains a statement of basis and purpose providing a clear explanation of the rule and requirements. The mayor's office of operations shall analyze: (a) plain language/readability; (b) whether drafting included analysis to minimize compliance costs for discrete regulated communities consistent with the rule's purpose; and (c) if establishing/modifying violations or penalties without a cure period, why no cure period or opportunity for ameliorative action was included. The certification and analysis must be annexed to the full text as published in the City Record, made public on the city's website, and transmitted to the speaker of the council. Rules subject to certain exceptions (emergency rules, monetary penalty changes, fee changes, or implementation of new mandates with minimal discretion) may be exempt from this review or have limited review; inadvertent failures do not invalidate rules and this subdivision creates no private right of action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for and consideration of public and agency comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall provide the public an opportunity to comment on the proposed rule through outreach to discrete regulated communities (if any), submission of written data/views/arguments, and at a public hearing unless the agency in writing determines a hearing would serve no public purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All written comments and a summary of oral comments received shall be placed in a public record and made readily available to the public within a reasonable time. After consideration of relevant comments, the agency may adopt a final rule; except for emergency rules, no final rule shall be adopted by a board or commission unless its final language is posted on the agency's website and electronically transmitted to each member of the board/commission at least three calendar days (exclusive of Sundays) prior to adoption; revisions may be made prior to vote if approved by unanimous consent. Consideration of comments and related requirements do not create a private right of action; inadvertent failure to comply does not invalidate a rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date, filing, and publication requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: No rule shall be effective until (a) filed by the agency with the corporation counsel for publication in the Compilation, (b) the rule and a statement of basis and purpose is transmitted to the council for its information, and (c) the rule and a statement of basis and purpose have been published in the City Record and thirty days have elapsed after such publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thirty-day delay may be waived where an agency makes a written finding of substantial need for earlier implementation and the mayor approves the finding before the effective date, and such finding/approval is contained in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication in Compilation and consequences of omission
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule shall be void if it is not published in the next supplement to the Compilation in which its publication is practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If publication was inadvertently omitted, the rule shall become effective as of its publication date if published within six months of the date the corporation counsel receives notice of its omission. Judicial or administrative actions commenced under such voided rules and pending prior to voidance may be prosecuted/defended to final effect as if the rule had not been voided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for rules and agency response timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may petition an agency to consider the adoption of any rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within sixty days after submission of a petition, the agency shall either deny the petition in writing stating reasons, or state the agency's intention to initiate rulemaking by a specified date concerning the petition's subject. Each agency must prescribe procedures for submission, consideration and disposition of petitions. For multi-member bodies, procedure rules may authorize delegation to the chair to reject petitions. Such agency decisions are within agency discretion and are not subject to judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance and public availability of written comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall establish a system for maintaining and making available for public inspection all written comments received in response to each notice of rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must preserve comment records and provide public access consistent with the public-record requirements set forth elsewhere in this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency rule adoption procedures and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may adopt a rule prior to the notice and comment otherwise required if immediate effectiveness is necessary to address an imminent threat to health, safety, property or a necessary service, provided the agency makes a written finding of such imminent threat and specific reasons which must be approved by the mayor before effectiveness (or by the elected official authorized to promulgate rules if not the mayor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule and accompanying finding must be made public forthwith and published in the City Record as soon as practicable, and transmitted electronically to the speaker, council legislative documents office, corporation counsel, each council member, chairs of community boards, news media and civic organizations no later than the date transmitted to the City Record. An emergency rule shall not remain in effect longer than sixty days unless the agency initiates notice-and-comment within that period and publishes a statement that an extension on an emergency basis is necessary for an additional sixty days; no further emergency finding may be made with respect to the same or a substantially similar rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and submission of previously adopted rules (sunset/review process)
rubrics_metrics.description: By specified dates following the chapter's effective date, each agency was required to send to the corporation counsel a copy of each rule in force as of a baseline date and identify each rule as: (a) to be continued in present form, (b) to be continued with amendments, or (c) to be repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment or repeal of such previously submitted rules is subject to the rulemaking provisions of section 1043. Corporation counsel must include such rules in the Compilation, with notations for rules identified for amendment or repeal. Rules in force as of the baseline date that were not submitted by the deadline shall have no force or effect after that deadline unless submitted. Any person may submit to an agency (within a specified period after Compilation publication) a copy or description of a rule believed to be in force; agencies shall endeavor to verify and, if appropriate, submit such rules to corporation counsel. Inadvertent failures and specified exceptions are addressed in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compilation of city rules: publication, certification, organization, and legal effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The corporation counsel shall publish a Compilation of city rules and keep it up to date through supplements at least every six months. The Compilation and its supplements shall be certified by the corporation counsel and shall include every rule currently in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Compilation may include other information deemed necessary for full understanding, shall be organized by agency and indexed by subject matter; an indexed edition was to be published by a specified date and updated every fourth year. Rules contained in the Compilation and its supplements, certified by corporation counsel, shall be the rules of the city unless added to, amended or repealed in accordance with section 1043. Materials in the Compilation may be edited, rearranged and updated for clarity/accuracy without change in substance; section numbers/stylistic/organizational non-substantive revisions become effective on publication. Documents submitted by agencies that were not formally adopted as rules may be included in the Compilation or filed in the municipal reference and research center and notice of such filing published in the City Record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication: notice of hearing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All parties shall be given reasonable notice of an adjudicative hearing, which shall include: (1) a statement of the nature of the proceeding and the time and place it will be held, if applicable; (2) a statement of the legal authority and jurisdiction under which the hearing is to be held, and a reference to the particular sections of law and rules involved; and (3) a short and plain statement of the matters to be adjudicated, including reference to the particular sections of law and rule involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies shall adopt rules governing procedures for adjudications and appeals and make such rules available upon request to any party who has received notice of violation/enforcement action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication: hearing rights and process
rubrics_metrics.description: At the hearing parties shall be afforded due process including the opportunity to be represented by counsel, to issue subpoenas or request issuance, to call witnesses, to cross-examine opposing witnesses, and to present oral and written arguments on law and facts. Adherence to formal rules of evidence is not required. No ex parte communications relating to other than ministerial matters shall be received by a hearing officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings of fact must be based exclusively on the record as a whole. Except as otherwise provided by state or local law, the party commencing the adjudication has the burden of proof. The hearing shall be transcribed or recorded; copies of transcript/record (or parts) must be made available to any party on request for a reasonable cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication: informal disposition and hearing officer role
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless precluded by law, informal disposition (ADR, stipulation, agreed settlement, consent order) may be made of any matter subject to adjudication. The person presiding at a hearing shall be assigned solely to adjudicative and related duties and, except as otherwise provided, shall make final findings of fact but shall not make any final decision, determination, or order; rather the hearing officer shall recommend such and forward the recommendation and record to the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency may adopt, reject or modify any recommended decision, determination or order. This separates fact-finding/recommending duties from the final decision-maker within the agency unless otherwise provided by charter or agency rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication: form and delivery of recommended or final decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any recommended decision, final decision, determination or order shall be in writing, or stated in the record if parties are present, and shall include findings of fact and conclusions of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of any written recommended decision, final decision, determination, or order shall be delivered or mailed forthwith to each party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaratory rulings
rubrics_metrics.description: On the written petition of any person, an agency may issue a written declaratory ruling on the applicability of any rule adopted by it to any person, property, or state of facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A declaratory ruling shall be binding only with respect to the person who makes the petition and only with respect to the stated facts contained in the petition.
